title: Pilot: per-vector time-decay batch discounts + rerank SLA addendum
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood has observed two common enterprise asks: lower per-vector effective cost for high-volume batch reranking jobs, and contractual clarity around rerank SLA and data handling for QSA/security questionnaires. Current per-vector pricing is simple but linear; customers pushing very large offline or nearline rerank pipelines want a predictable, lower unit cost without committing to long-term reserved capacity.

Proposal overview:
Run a 6-week pilot that introduces a time-decay batch discount model for embeddings/rerank workloads plus an accompanying contract addendum for enterprise QSA items. The time-decay batch discount grants backfilled credits for recent historical volume: customers get a nominal per-vector price but accumulate 'batch credits' that reduce effective unit cost for bursts that are density- and recency-weighted. Credits decay on a 30-day half-life to prevent permanent discount arbitrage. The pilot will be opt-in, applied to new invoices as a line-item called "Batch Credits (time-decay)".

Pricing mechanics (initial parameters):
- Base per-vector list price: $0.0009 per vector (existing baseline for pilot customers).
- Batch credit accrual: for each day a customer sends >X vectors (configurable threshold; pilot default X=5M), accrue credits equal to 10% of the overage volume toward the credit bucket.
- Credit redemption: when usage spikes in a billing period, credits reduce billed units at a 50% effective discount until credits exhausted.
- Decay: credits reduce by 50% every 30 days (exponential half-life).
- Monthly cap: credits can cover at most 70% of billed vectors in a month to protect revenue.

Rationale and trade-offs:
- Pros: creates visible economic benefit for bursty rerank customers without requiring multi-month commitments; aligns incentives for customers to smooth volume and for Redwood to recover revenue over time via decay and caps.
- Cons: increased billing complexity; requires accounting/finance changes and Console visibility. Risk of gaming via synthetic burst patterns—mitigated by recency decay and cap.

QSA / Contract addendum items:
We propose a short addendum template for pilot customers that covers rerank-specific QSA asks: data residency (specify VPC vs hosted), telemetry retention window for embeddings, encryption at rest and in transit, and a defined rerank SLO (p99 latency by model class + monthly error budget). Addendum will include:
- Explicit statement of data handling for batched rerank payloads (deleted after 30 days unless customer opts-in to caching).
- SLAs: availability and p99 latency bands for rerank endpoints; credits formula for SLA breaches.
- Security attestations: link to our SOC2 + sample KMS integration language and optional HSM offering.

Success metrics (pilot measurement):
- Commercial: net effective price reduction observed for pilot cohort (target average effective per-vector price drop >= 20% for burst months).
- Behavioral: at least 3 customers adopt pilot and run rerank batch pipelines >20M vectors/month within 6 weeks.
- Operational: Console shows credit buckets per customer, billing lines generated correctly, finance reconciliation within 3 days of invoice.
- Risk: no more than 2 instances of suspected gaming patterns across cohort.

Rollout plan:
1) Week 0-1: finalize mechanics with Finance and Billing; legal drafts addendum template; security prepares QSA clauses.
2) Week 2: instrument Console UI mock and billing prototype (ENG scope: billing line-item + credit ledger).
3) Week 3-4: run internal sandbox tests with synthetic workloads; security review.
4) Week 5-10: invite 3 pilot customers (1 enterprise, 1 mid-market, 1 AI-native) for opt-in pilot; start billing pilot month.
5) Week 11-12: evaluate metrics, iterate parameters; prepare scaling playbook or sunset.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Threshold X for accrual: default 5M is provisional; need Sales input on typical enterprise baselines.
- Credit accrual percentage and redemption multiplier: starts at 10% accrual and 50% redemption—finance wants alternatives to model revenue impact.
- SLA credit formula: product and legal to agree on per-incident credit caps for rerank p99 misses.
- Billing system changes: can we show an independent credit ledger on Console or only generate billing lines?

Artifacts / links:
- PRD (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/embeddings/batch-credits-time-decay (draft)
- Billing prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/2746 (WIP)
- Draft addendum (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1rERankQSA_Addendum_DRAFT

Acceptance criteria:
- Billing generates the "Batch Credits (time-decay)" line item and ledger entries for pilot accounts for two consecutive billing cycles.
- Console shows per-customer credit balance and a tooltip explaining decay rules.
- Legal signs off on addendum and Sales has a one-page sell sheet.
- Security/QSA checklist completed and sign-off logged in the ticket.

Notes for reviewers:
- Finance: attach revenue impact simulation for 12-month horizon with conservative/worst-case scenarios.
- Sales/SE: identify pilot candidate accounts and pre-brief legal on required QSA responses.
- Eng: minimal viable implementation can be ledger-based without realtime UI first; ensure idempotent credit accrual to handle replayed events.
